cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus (Romans 1:1), is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:7), and he calls them brothers. He's just spent chapters explaining how God saves people, and it ended with him breaking into praise (Romans 11:33-36). Now he turns it all toward everyday life, starting with one big word: Therefore.

cards.question: Paul says, "Therefore I urge you, brothers," and he gives the reason he's urging them. On account of what?

cards.text: Then Paul reaches for a word from the old altar: sacrifice. Now listen close to what he asks them to offer, friend.

cards.question: What does Paul urge the believers in Rome to offer to God as a sacrifice?

cards.text: Their bodies, offered as "living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God" in Paul's words. A sacrifice that wakes up, hits snooze, and is STILL a sacrifice.

cards.question: Paul says offering your body as a living sacrifice is your spiritual service of worship.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Do not be conformed to this world," and friend, I'm a cookie stamper. Pressing dough into my shape was my WHOLE job, so trust me when I say: don't let this world be your stamper.

cards.question: Instead of being conformed to this world, Paul says to be transformed. How?

answers.text: By the renewing of their mind
By the keeping of the law
By the strength of their will

cards.question: Paul says that with renewed minds, they'll be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing and perfect ___ of God.

cards.text: Next, Paul has a word for every one of the believers in Rome, and he says it by the grace given him.

cards.question: What does Paul tell every one of the believers in Rome not to do?

cards.text: Instead, Paul says to think of yourself with sober judgment. Friend, I shared a junk drawer with an expired coupon that STILL believed in itself. Sweetest coupon you ever met. Zero sober judgment.

cards.question: Paul says to think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of something God has given you. What is it?

cards.text: Then Paul points to something everyone carries around: one body with many parts, and not every part does the same job.

cards.question: Paul says that in Christ, the believers who are many are one what?
Paul says each member of the body of believers belongs only to himself.

cards.text: Each member belongs to one another. Friend, my gold base and I go EVERYWHERE together. I hop, it hops. I dive face-first into the chocolate chips, it dives in TOO.
Different parts, different jobs, and Paul says the believers have different gifts too.

cards.question: Paul writes that believers have different gifts according to the ___ given them.

cards.text: Then Paul runs a list: if your gift is prophecy, use it in proportion to your faith, and if it's serving, serve, and if it's teaching, teach. No meeting about the meeting, friend, just TEACH.
If your gift is encouraging, encourage. Then Paul keeps going, and for the next three gifts he says how, not just what.

cards.question: If a believer's gift is giving, how does Paul say to give?
Paul says the believer whose gift is leading should lead with diligence.
If a believer's gift is showing mercy, Paul says to do it ___.

findings.problem: The card says Paul has 'just spent chapters explaining how God saves people' and 'now he turns it all toward everyday life.' The first claim is a Bible fact with no reference. The second claims a connection between Romans 1-11 and chapter 12 that the text doesn't state.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to guess wording they haven't seen ('perfect ___ of God': will, word or law). No story card sets up testing and approving, so the baker can't reason it out. A baker could also argue that 'law' fits, since the law is called holy, righteous and good in Romans 7:12.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Story card 1 gives only 'by the grace given him,' which isn't enough context to reason toward 'Think too highly of themselves' over the other two answers. The pick is luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The joke makes the expired coupon, one of Papa Dorin's drawer friends, the butt of the joke ('Zero sober judgment'). He should be the one laughed at, not a friend.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself.

findings.problem: 'Different parts, different jobs' repeats what card 5 already told about verse 4. That recap is also why the card's citation reaches back to Romans 12:4. Its only new content is verse 6.

Asking how to give (generously, regularly or privately) makes the baker guess a detail of the wording. The setup only says Paul 'says how,' so the baker has nothing to reason from. This matches the Psalm 23 bad example of guessing a detail.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: 'Do it ___' (cheerfully, quietly or quickly) asks the baker to guess an unseen word of the line. Nothing told earlier lets them reason it out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
